items.headline: Fed minutes confirm hawkish September hike to 3.75%-4.00%, dot plot flags one more hike in 2026
items.summary: Minutes released Oct 7 from the Fed's Sept 15-16 meeting confirmed Chair Kevin Warsh led a unanimous 12-0 vote to raise rates 25bp to 3.75%-4.00% (first hike since 2023), citing elevated inflation. The September dot plot showed a majority of officials expecting another hike before year-end, more hawkish than markets had priced.
items.actionable: The hawkish Fed repricing is the single biggest macro risk to the silver/gold miner book and crypto exposure right now, so size and stop-loss decisions on GDX/SLVP/SILJ/AG should assume continued USD strength and yield pressure rather than an imminent pivot.

items.headline: Gold/silver slide as 10-year yield hits 24-year high and dollar strengthens
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield touched roughly 5.35% (highest since 2002) before easing to ~5.27%, while the DXY hit a fresh 2026 high near 102.5, pressuring gold (down to ~$4,109-4,131/oz) and silver (~$60/oz). The move extends a pullback from recent record highs as the hawkish Fed hike dented rate-cut hopes.
items.actionable: This is a yields/dollar-driven pullback, not a break in the physical silver deficit/squeeze thesis, so treat the GDX/SLVP/SILJ/AG drawdown as a macro correction to monitor rather than a fundamental sell signal, but expect continued volatility while the Fed stays hawkish.

items.headline: OCBC sheds 5.8% (~S$8b market cap) after Citi downgrade to Sell
items.summary: Citi cut OCBC from Neutral to Sell with a price target well below its pre-downgrade trading level, flagging flat Q3 YoY earnings, a 35-70bp net interest margin hit from repricing SGD fixed deposits, and 'misplaced optimism' on Singapore rates after OCBC's P/E expanded 46% this year. OCBC was the most heavily traded SGX stock that day at over S$459m turnover.
items.actionable: This resolves the previously unexplained OCBC drop: it is an analyst downgrade on NIM-compression and valuation grounds, not a credit event or regulatory action, so reassess the position on earnings/margin fundamentals rather than treating it as a red flag requiring an exit.

items.headline: China's rare-earth export-control truce nears Nov 10 expiry with no renewal signaled
items.summary: The one-year suspension of China's expanded rare-earth export controls (extraterritorial licensing, five added elements), agreed after the Oct 2025 Trump-Xi Busan summit, lapses Nov 10, 2026, and Beijing has given no public signal on renewal, narrowing, or letting it expire. Analysts estimate roughly $6.5 trillion of Western EV, chip and defense output is exposed if the fuller controls snap back.
items.actionable: A hard expiry without renewal would be a strong bullish catalyst for the rare-earth watchlist (MP Materials, Lynas, Energy Fuels) as Western buyers scramble for non-China supply -- worth setting a calendar alert for Nov 10.

items.headline: MP Materials to deliver GM's first non-China rare-earth magnets; Lynas inks ~$96m Pentagon offtake
items.summary: MP Materials is about to deliver General Motors' first rare-earth magnets made outside China, from its Texas facility, backed by the Pentagon's $400m preferred-equity stake, a $150m loan, and a 10-year commitment to buy NdPr output at a $110/kg floor. Separately, Lynas Rare Earths agreed to sell roughly $96m of light and heavy rare earths to the US Department of War over four years, referencing the same $110/kg NdPr floor.
items.actionable: Both watchlist names now have government-backed, price-floored revenue streams independent of spot rare-earth pricing, which de-risks the long thesis on MP/Lynas even if China eases export controls.

items.headline: Bitcoin sinks below $83K as yields/oil-driven risk-off triggers large liquidation cascade
items.summary: Bitcoin fell from roughly $86,600 to under $83,000 between Oct 6-7, with a rapid cascade wiping out hundreds of millions in long positions as rising Treasury yields and oil prices drove broad risk-off ahead of the Fed minutes. Glassnode flagged the spot market as 'fragile,' with a sustained move back above $85,000 looking difficult.
items.actionable: Crypto is trading as a high-beta risk-off proxy alongside gold/silver/equities right now rather than a safe haven -- the pullback mirrors the same hawkish-Fed/yields story hitting the miners, not a crypto-specific issue.

items.headline: Iran escalates Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks, pushing Brent above $100-102
items.summary: Iran has stepped up attacks on tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz, with nearly 20 commercial vessels hit over the past month, threatening the fragile rebound in Gulf oil exports through a waterway carrying roughly 20% of global seaborne oil. Brent traded above $100-102/bbl as a result, adding to the macro risk-off that also hit crypto and equities on Oct 6-7.
items.actionable: Higher, geopolitically-driven oil prices add inflation risk that could reinforce the Fed's hawkish tilt (a mild negative for gold/silver/risk assets broadly), with no direct read-through to SGX holdings beyond general risk sentiment.

items.headline: Hang Seng Tech slumps on AI-bubble jitters, down ~40% from Oct 2025 peak even as Nasdaq hits records
items.summary: The Hang Seng Index sank 2.6% to 23,972 on Oct 2 with financials and tech leading losses (Tencent -2.3%, Xiaomi -4%); the Hang Seng Tech sub-index has fallen almost 40% from its Oct 2025 peak, a sharp divergence from US AI-driven indices amid worries that China AI monetization is lagging the hardware/capex narrative.
items.actionable: The HK tech sell-off looks structural (a widening one-year AI-monetization gap versus the US), not a one-day event, so Tencent/Xiaomi/SMIC exposure should be sized for continued relative underperformance rather than an imminent bounce.

items.headline: Tencent and Xiaomi continue share buybacks amid tech selloff
items.summary: Tencent repurchased 238,000 shares on Oct 5 for HK$100m at HK$416.6-423.4, and Xiaomi bought back 2 million shares for HK$47.6m at HK$23.76-23.84, continuing active buyback programs even as Hong Kong tech names sold off on AI-bubble concerns.
items.actionable: Insider-level buyback support at these price levels is a modest offsetting signal that management sees current weakness as overdone, against the broader HK tech de-rating.

items.headline: Energy Fuels tumbles 9% as uranium/advanced-reactor names sell off together
items.summary: Energy Fuels (UUUU) fell 9% to $10.27, with Oklo and Centrus Energy down 5% each and the Global X Uranium ETF (URA) off 5%, even as the S&P 500 was roughly flat (-0.2%), indicating sector-specific selling tied to concerns that nuclear-buildout valuations are pricing in revenue that is still years away.
items.actionable: This explains the previously unexplained Energy Fuels drop as a uranium/nuclear-theme de-rating (Oklo, Centrus fell in tandem), not company-specific bad news, so it does not change the rare-earth/uranium diversification thesis but confirms high beta to nuclear-sector sentiment swings.

items.headline: No active US government shutdown -- stopgap funding runs to Dec 11, 2026
items.summary: A continuing resolution signed into law Sept 2, 2026 funds federal agencies through Dec 11, 2026, averting the widely-watched October shutdown risk; Congress is in recess until a Nov 9 lame-duck session where funding, LIHEAP and the farm bill must be resolved. Status reconfirmed as of this run.
items.actionable: Corrects a working assumption of an 'ongoing shutdown' carried in prior model.json driver text -- none is active right now, though the Dec 11 funding cliff remains worth re-flagging as that date approaches.
